audit.action: cite a better source for the same coding
audit.reasoning: The coding (fixed-dominant, final: '01 001 0001', stress on the ultima of the root) rests on Rhea 1995, a first-hand SIL sketch in the Comparative Austronesian Dictionary; the sentence is verbatim at section 2.1 in the now-fetched sources open file. An independent primary phonology article, Dean & Dean 1955 p.318 (open, fetched sources), gives the same rule ('primary stress normally... on the ultima of a word base') and adds secondary stress on the antepenult and variability in isolation forms; its informant is from the Koronadal area, so it is cross-dialect confirmation, and our koro1310 record already codes final from it (consistent). No grammar, phonology monograph or acoustic study of Blaan exists (Glottolog list; Bantilan et al. 2025 survey), so nothing on record suggests a different coding. Actions: (a) attach the fetched sources file and set an evidence grade (currently blank); (b) correct the citation

sources.quote: Stress in Blaan is predictable; it occurs on the ultimate syllable of the root word.

sources.citation: Dean, James & Gladys Dean. 1955. The phonemes of Bilaan. Philippine Journal of Science 84(3): 311-322. (archive.org pjs00317683vol84no3sep1955, open)
sources.quote: "A primary stress normally occurs on the ultima of a word base and a secondary stress on the antepenult of polysyllabic words." Footnote: "When words are given in isolation, out of normal context, stress may vary." Examples with accents on base-final syllables (dé, bukéy kudá ayé).
sources.locator: p. 318, section 'STRESS' and its footnote; informant locale p. 313 (Sitio Kablan, foot of Mt. Matutum = Koronadal Blaan area)
